why: The student wrote correct code that uses the running-extreme plan for the minimum. It starts at data[0], updates with Math.min in one pass over the array and prints the result after the loop. This is a familiar variant of the running-maximum program, so it is L3 rather than L4.

concepts.quote: double min = data[0]; for (double v : data) min = Math.min(min, v); System.out.println(min);
concepts.why: It finds the smallest value in one pass with one holder variable that starts at an actual data value, so the start value is safe. It is a slight variation of the familiar max plan.
Math.min is called with the class prefix and two double arguments, and its returned value is stored back in min.
